## kb_to_source

Sentence-level reverse scan of the 29 hub, baseline and factor documents of these four policies, their base-policy documents and the facets they read:
- Every obligation, eligibility, prohibition, calculation and ordering found has a structured source (rule, base rule, eligibility, overwrite replacement, factor ladder, parameter_schema/variant value or tool docstring). Worked examples are hypothetical and arithmetic-consistent.
- No added confirmation, review, notification, wait or failure procedure was found.
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each tool name appears only in its own hub.
- Task opening world state written as a policy fact: none (no document states that any customer has arrears, an unpaid most recent bill, a qualifying outage, etc.).
- Additions / rewrites / omissions: none that change entailment. See policy-side notes.

**Policy-side notes (reported, not KB verdicts):**
- PN-1 Governing schedule of the sustained-outage credit. Base `service_outage_credit_rule` keeps in force "The schedule in effect on the outage start date governs" (rendered in doc_service_sustained_outage_credit_terms "Governing schedule … even when the agreement has since moved to another schedule"). The baseline doc doc_service_sustained_credit_amount_method closes with "The schedule figures named above are those of the schedule the agreement is billed on", which has no rule-text home and follows the compute convention (`P()` reads the holding's current variant). The two readings diverge only when the schedule changed between the outage start and the posting, which is not triggered here (Schedule RS since 2016-05-02). Nature: an ambiguity between the in-force base clause and the extended compute; the KB surfaces both rather than hiding one.
- PN-2 Parameter glosses that restate retired clauses. doc_service_reconnection_charge_schedule_values carries the parameter_schema descriptions verbatim: "Reconnection payment basis — the amount that must be paid before a disconnected account is reconnected …", the three reconnection charges defined by restoration method and customer election, and "Standard reconnection hours — … worked at the standard charge". These are the semantics of the base clauses the two extended policies retired. The KB marks those clauses retired (doc_service_reconnection_requirements). The residue is in the source's parameter_schema, so this is not a KB defect. It did not change the blind answer.
- PN-3 The base claim-window clause ("must be requested no later than the claim window") stays in force next to the auto-posting replacement. The KB carries both as the source has them.

## dependency_form

- Prerequisite sentences: all three in this task's closure stand verbatim on the blocked side (card-payment hub ×2, order hub ×1). They keep their state form and connectives. The only restatements are same-form ones in the same documents: the card hub's "In terms of the agreement's records: … not yet fixed" and the order hub's item 2 "Put the other way round …". No depended-on document (LPC, sustained-outage or card-payment docs) carries the blocked side's sentence or names who waits on it.
- Tool names: each of the four tools appears only in its own hub. No route, checklist, roadmap or aggregated chain appears anywhere in the 73 docs. No document strings the LPC, the outage credit, the payment and the order into one procedure.
- Titles/openings: general subjects ("Card Payments toward Reconnection of a Disconnected Electric Service Agreement", "Reconnection Orders for Disconnected Electric Service Agreements", "Late Payment Charge … Posting Reference", "… Posting a Sustained-Outage Credit …"). Each `on_request` title names its policy's request type. None mirrors the task's situation.
- Computation documents: none says a variation exists. There is no "unless otherwise provided", no "adjustments may apply" and no pointer. Factor documents never name a tier a customer falls on and never point at the computation document.
- Non-RED observations, recorded for completeness:
  - doc_service_reconnection_charge_amount_field_services says "only the final reconnection charge is rounded to the cent" for a one-figure computation. This renders the source's assembly rounding clause and does not state a variation.
  - doc_service_door_hanger_field_visit_recovery_examples defines "the restoration charge … on which the reconnection charge rests" and gives a hypothetical restoration charge of 10.00 USD. The source's own ladder sentence ("A field-visit recovery is added to the restoration charge") names that quantity. The example is illustrative and does not point at the restoration-path document.
  - doc_service_repeat_lateness_late_charge_rate says "The repeat-lateness window is a stated number of calendar months". The months are stated only in the autopay-window factor document. This coupling between two factors is in the source (a method factor deciding the other factor's window). Neither document points at the other.
